InTempo Design System

The interface built for InTempo — a practice app that listens to a string player and tells them, measure by measure, whether they rushed or dragged. Warm paper, charcoal type, one gold accent, and hairlines instead of shadows. Every specimen below is set in the app's own faces at the app's own sizes.

  • 17 screens
  • 17 colour tokens
  • 10 type styles
  • 8 spacing steps

01 — Foundations

Colour, type, spacing, shape

These are the only values in the app. Every component below resolves to them; nothing declares a hex, a size, or a gap of its own. That rule is what keeps a system honest — a value that appears in one component and nowhere else is a decision nobody made.

Verdict colour

Quarantined to the verdict screen, and the restriction is the point: they never appear in chrome, navigation, buttons, tabs, or any surface that isn’t reporting how a take went. They are also never load-bearing — every coloured thing sits beside its own word, because red-green deficiency maps almost exactly onto this trio. Hues are the spec’s, darkened only as far as WCAG AA needed on this ground: the spec’s own amber measured 2.14:1 here, which its accessibility section forbids.

verdictOn#1D7F46On tempo. 4.50:1 — was #1F8A4C at 3.93.
verdictMid#8F681CSlight rush or drag. 4.50:1 — was #D69E2E at 2.14.
verdictBad#C53B3BRushing or dragging. 4.64:1, unchanged from the spec.

02 — Primitives

Sixteen pieces everything is built from

Specimens are life-size: 353 pt wide, which is a 393 pt phone less the 20 pt gutter either side. A component that only looks right at desktop width isn't the component that ships.

PageHeader

The serif screen title, with optional context above, an action beside it, and a back control for a pushed screen.

4 pages
Review pages

The back control is explicit, never automatic. iOS's swipe-back is real but invisible, Android's system back is a different affordance, and neither exists on the web build.

ScreenContainer

The screen shell: page ground, top safe-area inset, the 20 pt gutter, an optional pinned footer, and pull-to-refresh.

scroll area

The footer ends the scroll area rather than floating over it, so content clears it with no padding to keep in sync. Its rule appears only when there is something to scroll.

Card

The one card in the app: warm white on a hairline, no shadow.

default · radius 12 · padding 16
emphasis · radius 16
padded=false · content owns its insets

If a screen seems to need a different card, it needs this one with different content — not a second card style.

PrimaryButton

The one action that matters on a screen. Charcoal ground, ivory type, haptic on press.

Haptics route through one helper that reads the musician's setting, so the preference can't be honoured in one place and ignored in another.

SecondaryButton

The quieter action. Bordered, transparent fill, charcoal label.

Never two primaries on a screen. Where a pair is needed, the secondary leads and the primary closes.

IconButton

A bare glyph at the minimum comfortable target, for navigation and transport.

A label is required, not optional — an icon alone tells a screen reader nothing.

ProgressBar

A 4 pt track. One of the few places the accent appears.

value = null renders nothing at all

An empty track reads as "no progress yet", which is a different claim from "we don't know". So null renders nothing.

The only way type enters a screen. Ten variants, four colour roles, no ad-hoc sizes.

04 — Screen parts

Components that belong to one screen

Kept beside the screen that uses them rather than promoted into the shared system. A component used once is a detail of that screen; moving it into the system claims a generality it hasn't earned.

DeviationBar

How far a take sat from the beat, and which side of it.

Rushing · ahead of the beat
Slight drag · behind the beat
On tempo

Grows from a centre line because the quantity is signed — a left-anchored bar shows that someone drifted but not which side of the beat. Nothing is encoded in colour, so the verdict survives a colour-blind reading.

PieceInsightRow

One piece's tempo record: what it was, how it went, how often.

60 Studies for the Violin, Op. 45
Franz Wohlfahrt
Rushing  ·  12 sessions

Words carry the verdict, the bar carries the magnitude. No BPM figure — the spec keeps timing numbers out of production copy.

06 — Rules

The constraints that produced all of it

These are the part that doesn't survive a cold read of the code. Anyone extending this — or porting it to the web — needs them more than they need the hex values.

One accent, and it means something

Gold marks progress, the active tab, and links. It is never decoration, and there is no second accent to reach for.

Borders, not shadows

There is no elevation in the app. A card that needs to lift firms its border. This alone keeps it from reading as a generic SaaS surface.

The serif is reserved

Newsreader appears on works and screen titles only. Seeing it means you are looking at music, not at the app.

Numbers are dev-mode only

BPM offsets, percentages and millisecond deviations stay out of production copy. Words tell the musician what happened; the bar tells them how much. Session counts stay — a count of takes isn't a timing measurement.

One information system at a time

A list reads as words on every row or figures on every row, never a mix. The figure is a selection state: tapping a row selects it, and the selected row is the only one showing a number.

No scaffolding on a shipped screen

Missing dependencies, mocked data and unfinished plumbing are notes for whoever finishes them. The interface behaves as though the feature works; nothing tells a musician about the workshop behind it.

Verdict colour is quarantined

Green, amber and red exist, and appear on the verdict screen and nowhere else — not even on its headline, which stays charcoal. They sit on measure rows, where a musician is reading detail. Insights encodes nothing in colour: it summarises, it doesn’t judge a take. Verified by sweeping every other screen for the three values.

A take reports itself, a habit needs sessions

One recording says what happened and where — "You rushed in the middle", "Tempo drifted ahead". "You tend to…" is a claim about a habit, so it belongs to Insights, where there are sessions to average. The verdict screen never makes it.

A chart carries its own legend

Both axes are named on the chart rather than in a sentence beneath it. If prose is needed to read a chart, the chart is unfinished.

Never colour alone

Any verdict carries a word and, where it exists, an icon. Red–green deficiency maps almost exactly onto the verdict hues.

Musical language

"Ahead of the beat", not "early". "Behind the beat", not "late". "Rushing", not "positive tempo deviation". Sentence case throughout.

Nothing invented to fill a screen

No control ships without something behind it. Fields with no backing column are typed nullable so every component is forced to handle their absence.

Safe areas are measured, never assumed

Every top and bottom inset comes from what the device reports. There is not one hardcoded notch or status-bar offset in the app.

Motion is optional

Two durations, and every animated component reads reduce-motion — the OS setting and the in-app switch, OR'd, never substituted.

Drag is not accessible

Anything reorderable by gesture also exposes move-up and move-down actions.

The banned list

No gradients, neon, glassmorphism, purple-blue AI styling, sparkles, glowing buttons, badge clutter, decorative graphics, fake motivational copy, or uppercase labels.

Set in Newsreader and Inter — the app's own faces, embedded here rather than linked, so the specimens are the real thing and not an approximation.

Single theme by design: the app pins a light interface style and the palette is a warm ivory ground, so there is no dark token set to show and inventing one would misrepresent the system.

Recreated in HTML from the React Native source in mobile/. Where a specimen and the code disagree, the code is right.
